key_insight: A single, biomarker-agnostic plasma proteomics test using adaptive machine learning can distinguish malignant from benign adnexal masses with strong accuracy.
clinical_relevance: This approach could improve pre-operative triage beyond CA-125 or ultrasound alone and may reduce unnecessary surgery for women with adnexal masses.
method: Data-independent acquisition mass spectrometry measured >1,000 plasma proteins per sample.
ADAPT-MS retrained an ElasticNet classifier for each sample using the proteins detected.
Performance was tested across discovery, multiple validation cohorts, and an external validation center.
evidence_signal: Across five independent validation cohorts (n=623), the classifier achieved a summary AUC of 0.835, with higher performance when combined with O-RADS in matched subsets.
watch_item: The method depends on advanced mass spectrometry and multicenter validation, so broader real-world implementation and reproducibility still need confirmation.
paper_title: Differentiating benign from malignant adnexal masses by biomarker-agnostic plasma proteomics using adaptive machine learning
